Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১) Rotatory movement is used for the extraction of the :
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: The two teeth which can be removed by rotation only are maxillary central incisors and mandibular second premolar. (Ref-Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২) A pregnant patient in second trimester falls into syncope during extraction of upper molars. She should be kept in
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: The patient should not be kept in supine or reclined position to avoid pressure on inferior vena cava by the fetus, which results in poor venous return and hypotension. The patient is turned onto left side to relieve the pressure. (Ref-Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩) Reactionary hemorrhage occurs after extraction because of :
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Reactionary hemorrhage occurs within 24hours post-operatively due to rise of blood pressure or slipping of ligature. (Ref-Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৪) Displacement  of a root into the maxillary sinus during extraction is most likely to happen during the extraction of the maxillary :
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Usually the palatal root of maxillary first molar is present closer to maxillary sinus followed by maxillary second premolar, maxillary first premolar and last the maxillary second molar. (Ref- Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৫) Pain of dry socket is experienced on :
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Pain of dry socket is experienced on 3rd day after extraction. (Ref-Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৬) The ideal time for removal of impacted third molar is -
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option1: When the root formation has started
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option2: When the roots of the teeth are one-third formed and before they are two-thirds formed
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option3: When the roots of the teeth are two-thirds formed
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option4: When  the root formation is complete
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: The ideal time to remove an impacted wisdom tooth is when one-third to two-thirds of the root is formed, which generally corresponds with the middle to late teenage years.If it is removed too early, when no root is formed, the extraction process is difficult because the tooth tends to roll around in its bony crypt. If ,on the other hand,the roots are completely formed,the tooth is anchored firmly in place. (Ref- Critical decision in Periodontology by WALTER B. HALL)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৭) In WHARFE assessment of impacted third molars ‘A’ stands for
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: The six factors chosen for scoring in WHARFE assessments are-   Winter’s classification, Height of mandible, Angulation of third molar, Root shape, Follicle, Path of Exit of tooth during removal. (Ref-Srinivasan)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৮) Action of toxic doses of local anesthesia on CNS can be described as :
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option1: first stimulating  the CNS followed by depression
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option2: first depressing it followed by CNS stimulation
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Action of toxic doses of local anesthesia on CNS can be described as first stimulating the CNS followed by depression. (Ref-Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৯) It is difficult to obtain local infiltration anesthesia in the presence of inflammation because of :
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: It is difficult to obtain local infiltration anesthesia in the presence of inflammation because of decreased pH. (Ref- Monheim’s

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১০) Which of the following general anesthetic technique should be used for anesthesia in oral surgery :
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option4: IV anesthesia with nitrous oxide and oxygen
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Nasoendotracheal tube with throat pack general anesthetic technique should be used for anesthesia in oral surgery. (Ref- Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১১) The most common site of the fracture of the mandible is the
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Because of sudden change in angulation, angle is considered as weakest part of mandible. (Ref- Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১২) Eburnation is seen in
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Eburnation is seen in the case of non-union of fracture and the radiograph shows rounding off and sclerosis of bone ends. (Ref- Killey’s Mandibular Fracture)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১৩) The most common pathognomonic sign of mandibular fracture is
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option3: Deviation of the jaw on opening
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Sublingual ecchymosis is considered as pathognomonic sign of mandibular fracture. (Ref- Peterson)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১৪) Post -auricular ecchymosis in cases of fracture of the base of skull is called
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Post-auricular ecchymosis in cases of fracture of the base of skull is called Battle’s sign. (Ref- Killey’s Mandible Fracture)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১৫) Which of the following is not included in the Glassgow coma scale?
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Glassgow coma scale is used to know the level of consciousness of patient. It includes-Motor response, Verbal response, Eye opening. (Ref- Killyey’s Mid third fracture)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১৬) CSF rhinorrhea is found in :
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: CSF rhinorrhea is seen in nasoethmoidal, Le fort 2, Le fort 3 fractures associated with comminuted cribriform plate of ethmoid. Tramline effect and Halo on pillow effect are diagnostic signs of CSF rhinorrhea. (Ref-Killey’s Mid third Fracture)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১৭) ‘Panda facies’ is commonly seen after
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Panda facies is due to oedema and ecchymosis around the eyes.Because of this the patient develops black circles around the eyes(Raccoon eyes). (Ref-Neelima )

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১৮) The ‘Hanging drop appearance in the maxillary sinus radiograph indicates
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Hanging drop sign is best seen in the water projection of the face. (Ref- Killey’s Mid Third Fracture)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ১৯) Gillis approach is used in
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: The structure of anatomical significance  in Gillis approach is superficial temporal artery. (Ref-Killey’s Mid Third fracture)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২০) Hooding of eyes is seen in which fracture
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: IF fracture line passes above the Whitnall’s tubercle, it removes the support given to eye by Lockwood’s suspensory ligament and the upper eyelid follows the globe down producing hooding of eyes. (Ref- Killey’s Mid Third fracture)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২১) Frequent dislocation of TMJ is due to
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Spasm of muscle is responsible for acute dislocation.For frequent/recurrent dislocation, ligament and capsular flaccidity,flattening of articular eminence and trauma are the causative triad.( Ref-Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২২) In dislocation of the jaw, displacement of the articular disc beyond the articular tubercle of the TMJ results from spasm or excessive constriction of the following muscle?
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: In dislocation of the jaw, displacement of the articular disc beyond the articular tubercle of the TMJ results from spasm or excessive constriction of lateral pterygoid muscle. (Ref- Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২৩) Unilateral TMJ ankylosis is associated with the following features, except:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option2: Facial asymmetry with fullness on the normal side of mandible
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option3: Chin deviated towards the affected side
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option4: Prominent antegonial notch on the affected side
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: In unilateral TMJ ankylosis , face is asymmetrical with fullness on the affected side of mandible and flattening on the normal side. (Ref-Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২৪) For a 8 year old child with TMJ ankylosis , the treatment of choice is
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Autogenous costochondral graft acts as a growth centre to the TMJ area to provide future growth of mandible. A minimum of 1.5cm of chondral graft is harvested through the inframammary region. Either 6th or 7th rib is harvested. (Ref-Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২৫) Most common cause of clicking:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Disk displacement with reduction is more common than disk displacement without reduction. Disk displacement with reduction typically causes clicking and pain with chewing. (Ref- Burket’s)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২৬) Which of the following is not an advantage of marsupialization?
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Marsupialization involves  de roofing of cyst along with adjoining bone and mucoperiosteum so that the cystic lining becomes continuous with oral epithelium.It is indicated in excessively large cyst. (Ref-Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২৭) The aspirate from a keratocyst will have:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: A low protein content of less than of 4 gm/dl is typical for keratocyst.All other cysts will have protein content of 5-11 gm/dl which is equal to mean protein level of serum. (Ref-Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২৮) A empty cavity in the mandible with no lining is mostly likely to be:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Stafne’s idiopathic bone cavity is located below mandibular canal and yields air on aspiration. (Ref- Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ২৯) The most appropriate method to differentiate between a dentigerous cyst and an ameloblastoma is through:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Microscopic examination is the most appropriate method to differentiate between a dentigerous cyst and an ameloblastoma. (Ref-Neelima

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩০) Treatment of Fibrous dysplasia is:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option3: if the lesion is small, dissection is done; if lesion is large, cosmetic surgery has to be carried out
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Treatment of fibrous dysplasia is -if the lesion is small, dissection is done; if lesion is large, cosmetic surgery has to be carried out. (Ref-Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩১) Garre's osteomyelitis
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option1: Chronic focal sclerosis and non-suppurative osteomyelitis
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option2: Chronic focal sclerosis and suppurative osteomyelitis
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option3: characterized by suppuration and acute pain
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Garre’s osteomyelitis characteristically shows proliferative periostitis where there is peripheral subperiosteal bone deposition caused by mild irritation and infection. ( Ref-Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩২) Which of the following is not a primary mandibular space:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Primary mandibular spaces are – submental space, sublingual space, submandibular space, Buccal space. (Ref- Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩৩) Death in ludwig’s angina occurs due to
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp:
In Ludwig's angina, there is progressive dyspnoea due to backward spread of infection. If not treated,it results in edema of glottis and causes complete respiratory obstruction.
(Ref-Neelima,Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩৪) Osteomyelitis
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option2: In acute cases fracture mandible is very common
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.option3: Of mandible can show symptoms of lip paraesthesia
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Osteomyelitis of mandible can show symptoms of lip paraesthesia. (Ref- Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩৫) Dead bone is seen on the X-ray as:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: In osteomyelitis, Dead bone is seen on the x-ray as more radiopaque. (Ref - Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩৬) which of the following is a secondary site of spread of odontogenic infection involving pterygomandibular space infection?
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: The sites of secondary infection from pterygomandibular space infections are- Infratemporal space, Retropharyngeal space, Buccal space and submandibular space. (Ref-Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩৭) Surgical recontouring of alveolar ridge is called as
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp:
Alveoloplasty is performed following multiple extractions for proper wound closure and for removal of undercut areas.

Alveolectomy refers to surgical removal or trimming of alveolar process.The main aim of alveolectomy is to prepare a good bed for denture. (Ref- Neelima, Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩৮) V-Y plasty procedure is used for
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: V-Y plasty procedure is used for frenectomy procedure to increase the stability of denture. (Ref- Neelima)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৩৯) Poor accessibility is the main disadvantage of which flap:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Poor accessibility is the main disadvantage of semilunar flap. (Ref- Vinod Kapoor)

Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.question: ৪০) Abbey-Estlander flap is used in the reconstruction of:
Oral Surgery and Anaesthesia.exp: Abbey-Estlander flap is used in the reconstruction of lip. (Ref- Stell_Marans)
